content:
One of the constructs invented when generalizing the real interpolation theorem to enorms was ENormedSpace. This notion has not been upstreamed to mathlib so far, and deciding about its fate is blocking upstreaming all of WeakType.lean.

Looking at the situation again today, I realize that the concept is now superfluous, because the process of generalizing mathlib to enorms led to docs#ENormSMulClass being added to mathlib: [ENormedSpace E] is equivalent to [ENormedAddCommMonoid E] [Module ℝ≥0 E] [ENormSMulClass ℝ≥0 E].
carleson#629 goes through all occurrences of ENormedSpace and replaces them with this combination (or some weaker typeclasses, when these suffice).

I should think that one argument for "should we have X" is "is X studied a lot in actual mathematics" -- and are Enormed spaces? The normed algebra hierarchy is already large and sometimes leads to bad slowdowns. Why expand it if we don't need it? I guess that would be an argument against it.

I used to think that it was all about "if we can think of one use for it, let's have it" but having stared at many typeclass traces in the past I can see arguments for only expanding the hierarchy if it fills a mathematical need. I guess it's swings and roundabouts?

Example of filling a need: we have [NumberField F] even though it was possible to express this concept with other Prop-valued typeclasses, because at the end of the day a lot of people say "let F be a number field". Do lots of people say "let V be an Enormed space"?
